NVIDIA is a semiconductor company founded in 1993, best known for designing graphics processing units (GPUs) that power gaming, professional visualisation, and artificial intelligence. It trades on NASDAQ under the ticker NVDA.

**What it does:**
NVIDIA designs GPUs and the surrounding software ecosystem. Its chips accelerate workloads from real-time graphics to large-scale machine learning, and its CUDA software platform has become the de facto standard for general-purpose GPU computing. The company sells into gaming, data centres, professional visualisation, and automotive markets.

**Core strategy:**
NVIDIA's long bet was that parallel computation on GPUs would matter far beyond graphics. That bet paid off as machine learning came to rely on the massive parallelism GPUs provide, making NVIDIA a central supplier of the hardware behind modern AI.

**Market position:**
NVIDIA became one of the most valuable companies in the world on the back of demand for AI accelerators, joining the small group of US firms to cross multi-trillion-dollar valuations. Its data-centre business now rivals or exceeds its historical gaming roots, and its results are widely watched as a barometer for AI infrastructure spending.

The company develops, licenses, and supports software, services, devices, and cloud infrastructure. Its best-known products include the Windows operating system, the Office and Microsoft 365 productivity suite, the Azure cloud platform, the Xbox gaming business, and the LinkedIn professional network.
